question.text: An anchor LP of 'Brahmaputra Infra AIF' negotiates a 'Most Favoured Nation' (MFN) clause in its side letter. What does an MFN clause primarily allow the investor to do?

answer.text: Receive side letter entitlements that protect against less favourable terms/conditions compared to those offered to other current or future investors
Redeem units before the lock-in period without paying exit load
Get a guaranteed minimum IRR of the hurdle rate
Demand appointment of the investor's nominee as the trustee

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.4.1, an MFN clause allows an investor to receive side-letter entitlements that protect against less favourable terms or conditions in the PPM compared to those offered to other current or future investors. It is fundamentally a parity-protection mechanism. The Trap: Redeeming units before the lock-in period without exit load relates to liquidity rights, not MFN. A guaranteed minimum IRR at the hurdle rate would be a return guarantee, which the MFN does not provide. Demanding appointment of the investor's nominee as trustee is a governance right, not a parity right. Note: MFN is purely a parity mechanism for side-letter entitlements; it is neither a return guarantee nor a governance appointment right.
